The test image shows a tomato stem cut longitudinally, revealing:
- Extensive dark brown to black discoloration throughout the pith/vascular tissue
- An external canker/lesion visible on the left side of the stem (near soil line)
- The cortex remains somewhat green while the interior is heavily necrotic

This points to a stem disease with internal dark discoloration. Top candidates: **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers** (dark cankers with pith browning/cracking) or **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (longitudinal stem slicing for diagnosis).

Let me view the Alternaria stem reference.

The Alternaria reference shows an external stem canker near the soil line, but the test image shows a longitudinally sliced stem revealing the internal pith damage. The key match points:

**Test image features:**
- Large dark external canker visible on left (near soil line)
- Internal pith shows extensive dark brown to **almost black** discoloration
- Cracked, dry-looking pith tissue
- Damage extends along the length of the stem

**Alternaria match:** The KB description specifically states "Vascular and pith tissue directly above and below cankers develop **brown streaks and become cracked and dry**" and "dark-brown to almost black cankers." The external canker visible on the left side of the test image combined with the dark internal pith matches Alternaria stem canker cut open for examination.

Sclerotinia would show distinct hard black sclerotia embedded in the stem and/or white mycelium — neither visible here. Verticillium wilt vascular discoloration is typically lighter brown, not this dark/black.
